current_law_statement: Sources: owner-supplied official texts of RCW 42.56.120 (apps.leg.wa.gov page fetched 2026-08-20; history ends 2017 c 304 s 3) and RCW 42.56.070 (certified PDF, certified 7/15/2026; history ends 2017 c 304 s 1) — both current codified text. RCW 42.56.520 opened on the web 2026-08-20 (history ends 2017 c 303 s 3 — no fee/deposit clock content). RCW 42.56.240 opened on the web 2026-08-20; its (14)(f) body-cam redaction-cost charge is current with history through 2026 c 174 s 6. Recency check (2024-2026): web search + the 2026-08-20 official .120 page and the 7/15/2026 certified .070 PDF show NO 2024-2026 amendments to the fee sections (.070/.120); .240 was amended through 2026 but (14)(f) redaction-cost language is present in the current text. Guidance-vs-law gap: the AG model rules (chapter 44-14 WAC, adopted under RCW 42.56.570) are advisory for agencies, not binding law; WAC 44-14-07001 was opened and restates the statutory charges (incl. the 2(f) summary-of-charges duty) without adding operative figures. Chapter 42.56 'agency' includes every state and local agency, so all figures below bind municipalities directly (all_public_bodies).

resolutions.source_language: To the extent the agency has not determined the actual costs of copying public records, the agency may not charge in excess of: (i) Fifteen cents per page for photocopies of public records, printed copies of electronic public records when requested by the person requesting records, or for the use of agency equipment to photocopy public records;
resolutions.notes: Default ceiling applies only where the agency has NOT determined/published actual costs (and has rules declaring why calculating them would be unduly burdensome, 120(2)(b)). An agency that publishes actual costs under RCW 42.56.070(7) is capped at that published actual cost instead (120(2)(a)); adoption requires notice and public hearing (WA-9008). Binds municipalities directly — chapter 42.56 'agency' includes local agencies.

resolutions.source_language: To the extent the agency has not determined the actual costs of copying public records, the agency may not charge in excess of: (i) Fifteen cents per page for photocopies of public records, printed copies of electronic public records when requested by the person requesting records, or for the use of agency equipment to photocopy public records;
resolutions.manual_verification: Scope judgment: the statute sets no color-specific rate; the generic 'photocopies' default was applied to color copies.
resolutions.notes: No color-specific rate anywhere in RCW 42.56.120 or the AG model rules opened. The 15-cent photocopy default is not limited by color, so it governs color pages under the default schedule; an agency wanting a higher color rate must publish an actual-cost statement (RCW 42.56.070(7)) and charge no more than actual cost.

resolutions.source_language: A reasonable charge may be imposed for providing copies of public records and for the use by any person of agency equipment or equipment of the office of the secretary of the senate or the office of the chief clerk of the house of representatives to copy public records, which charges shall not exceed the amount necessary to reimburse the agency, the office of the secretary of the senate, or the office of the chief clerk of the house of representatives for its actual costs directly incident to such copying.
resolutions.manual_verification: Judgment call: no oversized/nonstandard-specific rate exists; resolved to the general actual-cost standard.
resolutions.notes: Standard verbatim: 'reasonable charge ... shall not exceed ... actual costs directly incident to such copying'. The default 15-cent photocopy ceiling (120(2)(b)(i)) does not distinguish page size; an agency reproducing oversized formats at higher cost must publish an actual-cost statement (WA-0027) to charge more.

resolutions.source_language: The customized service charge may reimburse the agency up to the actual cost of providing the services in this subsection.
resolutions.notes: Customized service charge: standard = actual cost of providing the service, and only for requests requiring IT expertise for data compilations or customized electronic access not used for other agency purposes; conditioned on advance notice with explanation, description of expertise, and a reasonable cost estimate (120(3)(b), WA-9001). WA-9001 replaces the paraphrased WA-0029 with verbatim text.

Coverage: full text of RCW 42.56.120 and 42.56.070(7) read (owner-supplied official texts); WAC 44-14-07001 (AG model rule on charges) opened. No graduated page bands anywhere — the default rates are flat per-page/per-unit ceilings and may be combined (120(2)(c)). Absence of a found rule, not proof none exists in a non-fee chapter.

No numeric free-page allowance in RCW 42.56.120/.070 or WAC 44-14-07001. Related zero-charge categories exist but are categorical, not page counts: inspection and locating are free (120(1), WA-9005) and no copying charge for records routinely posted on the agency website (120(2)(e), WA-0026). Cities may adopt a free-page allowance by local rule; the state sets none.

resolutions.source_language: No fee shall be charged for the inspection of public records or locating public documents and making them available for copying, except as provided in RCW 42.56.240(14) and subsection (3) of this section.
resolutions.notes: Search/retrieval labor is categorically non-chargeable in WA — a search labor rate cannot exist. Two statutory exceptions: body-worn-camera redaction costs for non-exempt requesters (RCW 42.56.240(14)(f), WA-9007) and the customized service charge for IT-expertise compilations (120(3), WA-9001).

resolutions.source_language: No fee shall be charged for the inspection of public records or locating public documents and making them available for copying, except as provided in RCW 42.56.240(14) and subsection (3) of this section.
resolutions.manual_verification: Review/redaction is not named expressly; non-chargeability is the combined effect of 120(1) (only copying may be charged, at actual costs directly incident to copying) and 070(7)(b) (no staff salaries/benefits/overhead unless directly related to the actual cost of copying).
resolutions.notes: General review/redaction labor is not chargeable: the only permitted charges are copying charges capped at actual costs directly incident to copying, and staff salaries are excluded from that calculation except time to copy and send (070(7)(b), WA-9009). Statutory exception: reasonable costs of redacting body-worn-camera recordings may be charged to requesters not exempt under 240(14)(e) (WA-9007).

resolutions.source_language: A customized service charge may only be imposed if the agency estimates that the request would require the use of information technology expertise to prepare data compilations, or provide customized electronic access services when such compilations and customized access services are not used by the agency for other agency purposes. (ii) The customized service charge may reimburse the agency up to the actual cost of providing the services in this subsection.
resolutions.notes: Programming/data-extraction labor is chargeable only as the customized service charge — up to actual cost, no hourly figure in statute; the city sets its rate within actual cost. Gate: advance notice with explanation, description of the specific expertise, and a reasonable cost estimate, plus opportunity to amend the request (120(3)(b)).

resolutions.source_language: Staff time to copy and send the requested public records may be included in an agency's costs.
resolutions.notes: Shape of the gate: (a) NEVER chargeable — inspection, locating, review/redaction generally (120(1), WA-9005; 070(7)(b) excludes staff salaries/overhead, WA-0028); (b) chargeable within published actual copy costs — staff time to copy and send only (070(7)(b) last sentence, WA-9009); (c) chargeable with notice gate — IT customized service charge up to actual cost (120(3), WA-9001); (d) chargeable to non-exempt requesters — body-cam redaction costs (240(14)(f), WA-9007). No page/hour threshold and no paper-only scope.

resolutions.source_language: In determining the actual costs for providing copies of public records, an agency may not include staff salaries, benefits, or other general administrative or overhead charges, unless those costs are directly related to the actual cost of copying the public records.
resolutions.notes: An overhead/fringe percentage surcharge cannot exist under WA law — general administrative or overhead charges and benefits are expressly excluded from the actual-cost calculation unless directly related to the actual cost of copying. Certified 7/15/2026 text.

Coverage: RCW 42.56.120 and 42.56.070(7) full text read; WAC 44-14-07001 opened. No billing-increment or rounding rule. Largely moot because hourly labor billing barely exists in WA (search labor non-chargeable; copy-and-send time folded into actual copy cost).

No free-labor-hours allowance in the fee sections — and none is needed for search labor, which is categorically free (WA-9005). No free allowance is stated for the chargeable slivers (copy-and-send time, customized service charge, body-cam redaction).

No TX-§552.275-style per-requestor periodic free-time counter in chapter 42.56. Note: RCW 42.56.240(14)(f)(iii) acknowledges that agencies may have an 'allocation of, or limitation on, time or costs spent responding to public records requests ... established pursuant to local ordinance, policy, procedure, or state law' — i.e., monthly time allocations exist in WA as LOCAL policy, not a state figure. Statute recognizes but does not create or bound them.

resolutions.source_language: A requestor may ask an agency to provide, and if requested an agency shall provide, a summary of the applicable charges before any copies are made and the requestor may revise the request to reduce the number of copies to be made and reduce the applicable charges.
resolutions.notes: No dollar or hour threshold. Two gates instead: (1) ON REQUEST, a summary of applicable charges is mandatory before any copies are made, with a right to revise the request (2)(f), WA-9006); (2) a customized service charge may NEVER be assessed without advance notice including an explanation, description of expertise, and a reasonable cost estimate (3)(b), WA-9001). Engine shape: threshold = none; notice duties are trigger-based.

Coverage: RCW 42.56.120(4) (deposits/installments/waiver), full text of RCW 42.56.520 (5-business-day response; clarification nonresponse in 520(3)(b) applies to CLARIFICATION, not estimates), and WAC 44-14-07001 all opened — no N-day requester response window for a fee estimate. The only statutory abandonment trigger is the unclaimed-installment rule (120(4), WA-9002), which carries no day count. Cities set the window by local rule.

No revised-estimate-on-variance percentage anywhere in the fee sections, 42.56.520, or WAC 44-14-07001. The customized-service-charge notice (120(3)(b)) requires 'a reasonable estimate cost of the charge' up front but sets no overrun-revision duty.
No estimate validity period in RCW 42.56.120, 42.56.070(7), 42.56.520, or WAC 44-14-07001.

No dollar threshold: RCW 42.56.120(4) permits a deposit for ANY request regardless of estimated amount, bounded only by the 10% cap (see rules.deposit.percent / WA-0031). A city may set its own trigger threshold by local rule; the state sets none.

resolutions.unit: percent of the estimated cost of providing copies (including any customized service charge)
resolutions.source_language: An agency may require a deposit in an amount not to exceed ten percent of the estimated cost of providing copies for a request, including a customized service charge.
resolutions.notes: Ceiling of 10% of the estimate; the city sets the operative deposit percentage at or under it. The owner-supplied official text confirms the base includes a customized service charge (detail absent from WA-0031's summary).

resolutions.source_language: If an agency makes a request available on a partial or installment basis, the agency may charge for each part of the request as it is provided.
resolutions.notes: Gate shape: (1) up-front deposit up to 10% of the estimate before providing copies (WA-0031); (2) pay-per-installment — the agency may charge for each part as it is provided, and an unclaimed/unreviewed installment ends the duty to fulfill the balance (WA-9002). The statute does not expressly authorize withholding a completed non-installment production until full payment, but the installment mechanism plus per-part charging is the statutory payment gate.

resolutions.source_language: If an installment of a records request is not claimed or reviewed, the agency is not obligated to fulfill the balance of the request.
resolutions.notes: Terminal trigger with NO statutory day count — the grace period before treating an installment as unclaimed is a city policy choice. No prior-debt-prepayment provision exists in chapter 42.56. WA-9002 supplies the verbatim clause that WA-0032 carried only as a paraphrase.

Coverage: full text of RCW 42.56.520 (fetched 2026-08-20; history ends 2017 c 303) and 42.56.120(4) — neither addresses the statutory clock while a deposit is unpaid, a grace period, or a lapse action. WA's response deadline regime uses a 'reasonable estimate of the time' (520(1)(c)) rather than a fixed production clock, so in practice agencies condition further processing on the deposit by local rule; the statute is silent.
No overrun re-issue rule (revised estimate required / collection blocked / window restarted) in RCW 42.56.120, .070(7), .520, or WAC 44-14-07001.
out of scope per owner decision 2026-08-20 — finance-department policy, excluded from state rules profile

resolutions.source_language: A reasonable charge may be imposed for providing copies of public records and for the use by any person of agency equipment or equipment of the office of the secretary of the senate or the office of the chief clerk of the house of representatives to copy public records, which charges shall not exceed the amount necessary to reimburse the agency, the office of the secretary of the senate, or the office of the chief clerk of the house of representatives for its actual costs directly incident to such copying.
resolutions.notes: Request-level cap = actual costs directly incident to copying, using the most reasonable cost-efficient method (120(1)); per-page charges may never exceed the agency's published actual cost (120(2)(a)); actual-cost charging requires an adopted, published statement of costs preceded by notice and public hearing (070(7), WA-9008). Alternative: the $2 flat fee in lieu of itemized charges (120(2)(d), WA-0025).

No statutory de-minimis dollar floor below which charging is barred. Related but distinct: the $2 flat fee (120(2)(d)) is an OPTIONAL alternative available only when documented costs are clearly >= $2 — it is not a de-minimis waiver; and agencies hold general discretionary waiver authority under their own rules (120(4), WA-9003), which is how WA cities typically implement a de-minimis threshold.

No minimum fee. The $2 flat fee (120(2)(d), WA-0025) is a capped alternative charging mode, not a minimum — and charging it on an initial installment forecloses per-unit fees on later installments of the same request.

resolutions.source_language: The actual cost of any digital storage media or device provided by the agency, the actual cost of any container or envelope used to mail the copies to the requestor, and the actual postage or delivery charge.
resolutions.notes: CD/DVD/USB and other digital storage media/devices: chargeable at ACTUAL COST under the default schedule (no fixed dollar figure). Electronic delivery instead has numeric defaults: five cents per each four electronic files uploaded (b)(iii), WA-0023) and ten cents per gigabyte transmitted ((b)(iv), WA-0024). Charges under (b) may be combined ((c)).

resolutions.source_language: The actual cost of any digital storage media or device provided by the agency, the actual cost of any container or envelope used to mail the copies to the requestor, and the actual postage or delivery charge.
resolutions.notes: Mail delivery: actual cost of container/envelope plus actual postage or delivery charge ((b)(v), WA-9010). Electronic delivery defaults (absent published actual costs): 5 cents per each four files/attachments uploaded ((b)(iii)) and 10 cents per gigabyte transmitted ((b)(iv)); agency must use the most efficient manner available in its normal operations. No pickup charge exists (inspection is free, 120(1)).

resolutions.manual_verification: Officer-specific certified-copy fee statutes outside chapter 42.56 (e.g., county clerk fee schedules) were not exhaustively inventoried; they are record-type-specific, not general municipal PRA rules.
resolutions.notes: The PRA fee sections (42.56.120, 42.56.070(7)) contain no certification or certified-copy charge. Certified-copy fees in Washington live in officer-specific fee statutes outside the PRA and vary by record type; for a general municipal public-records request the state sets no certification fee.

resolutions.source_language: A law enforcement or corrections agency responding to a request to disclose body worn camera recordings may require any requester not listed in (e) of this subsection to pay the reasonable costs of redacting, altering, distorting, pixelating, suppressing, or otherwise obscuring any portion of the body worn camera recording prior to disclosure only to the extent necessary to comply with the exemptions in this chapter or any applicable law.
resolutions.manual_verification: 240(14)(f) text extracted from the official RCW page via retrieval tool (two consistent fetches, 2026-08-20); .240 was amended through 2026 c 174 — verify (14)(f) wording against the certified text in the verify pass.
resolutions.notes: No per-recording, per-minute, or free-minutes figures anywhere in WA law. AV copies fall under the general electronic defaults (10 cents/GB transmission, actual cost of media). The one AV-specific charge is structural: law-enforcement/corrections agencies (incl. municipal police) may charge non-exempt requesters the reasonable costs of redacting body-worn-camera recordings, using the least costly commercially available redaction method (240(14)(f), WA-9007); requesters listed in 240(14)(e) (persons in the recording, their attorneys, etc.) are exempt.

resolutions.source_language: This chapter shall not be construed as giving authority to any agency, the office of the secretary of the senate, or the office of the chief clerk of the house of representatives to give, sell or provide access to lists of individuals requested for commercial purposes, and agencies, the office of the secretary of the senate, and the office of the chief clerk of the house of representatives shall not do so unless specifically authorized or directed by law: PROVIDED, HOWEVER, That lists of applicants for professional licenses and of professional licensees shall be made available to those professional associations or educational organizations recognized by their professional licensing or examination board, upon payment of a reasonable charge therefor
resolutions.notes: WA has NO commercial-purpose fee schedule or surcharge — the commercial branch is a PROHIBITION: lists of individuals requested for commercial purposes may not be provided at all unless specifically authorized by law (with the professional-license-list proviso at a 'reasonable charge'). Engine shape: commercial purpose gates DENIAL of list requests, not a fee multiplier. Verbatim from the certified 7/15/2026 text.

resolutions.source_language: An agency may waive any charge assessed for a request pursuant to agency rules and regulations.
resolutions.notes: Waiver is fully discretionary and expressly delegated to the agency's own rules and regulations — the city defines grounds. The statute names no mandatory grounds, no indigency/public-interest test, no purpose statement, no written-denial duty, and no waiver-specific appeal. Also available: alternative fee arrangements by contract/MOU (WA-9004).

No fee-forfeiture-on-late-response rule in RCW 42.56.120, .070, or .520. WA's late-response consequences run through penalties/attorney fees in RCW 42.56.550 (enforcement, out of fee scope), not fee forfeiture.

resolutions.source_language: An agency may enter into any contract, memorandum of understanding, or other agreement with a requestor that provides an alternative fee arrangement to the charges authorized in this section, or in response to a voluminous or frequently occurring request.
resolutions.notes: No carry-forward or aggregation threshold. The statutory tool for repeat/voluminous requestors is a negotiated alternative fee arrangement (contract/MOU) — a structural path, not a value. RCW 42.56.240(14)(f)(iii) additionally acknowledges local time/cost allocations for records responses established by local ordinance or policy.

new_rules.atomic_rule: An agency may add a customized service charge, up to the actual cost of the services, only when the request requires IT expertise for data compilations or customized electronic access not used for other agency purposes, and only after notice to the requestor with an explanation, a description of the expertise, a reasonable cost estimate, and an opportunity to amend the request.
new_rules.trigger: Request requires information technology expertise to prepare data compilations or provide customized electronic access services not used by the agency for other agency purposes.
new_rules.source_language: (3)(a)(i) In addition to the charge imposed for providing copies of public records and for the use by any person of agency equipment copying costs, an agency may include a customized service charge. A customized service charge may only be imposed if the agency estimates that the request would require the use of information technology expertise to prepare data compilations, or provide customized electronic access services when such compilations and customized access services are not used by the agency for other agency purposes. (ii) The customized service charge may reimburse the agency up to the actual cost of providing the services in this subsection. (b) An agency may not assess a customized service charge unless the agency has notified the requestor of the customized service charge to be applied to the request, including an explanation of why the customized service charge applies, a description of the specific expertise, and a reasonable estimate cost of the charge. The notice also must provide the requestor the opportunity to amend his or her request in order to avoid or reduce the cost of a customized service charge.
new_rules.notes: Amends WA-0029, which carried only a paraphrase flagged 'Requires manual verification' — verbatim text now confirmed from the owner-supplied official 42.56.120 page (fetched 2026-08-20). The deposit base includes this charge (120(4)).

new_rules.legal_concept: Installment charging; unclaimed installment ends duty
new_rules.atomic_rule: An agency providing a request on a partial or installment basis may charge for each part as it is provided; if an installment is not claimed or reviewed, the agency is not obligated to fulfill the balance of the request.
new_rules.trigger: Request produced on a partial or installment basis; an installment goes unclaimed or unreviewed.
new_rules.clock_spec: terminal: duty to fulfill the balance ends when an installment is not claimed or reviewed (no statutory day count)
new_rules.source_language: If an agency makes a request available on a partial or installment basis, the agency may charge for each part of the request as it is provided. If an installment of a records request is not claimed or reviewed, the agency is not obligated to fulfill the balance of the request.
new_rules.notes: Amends WA-0032 (was a paraphrase flagged 'Requires manual verification'); verbatim confirmed from the owner-supplied official text. No grace-period day count — that is a local-policy choice.

new_rules.legal_concept: Discretionary fee waiver per agency rules
new_rules.atomic_rule: An agency may waive any charge assessed for a request, pursuant to the agency's own rules and regulations.
new_rules.trigger: Agency elects to waive a charge under its adopted rules.
new_rules.source_language: An agency may waive any charge assessed for a request pursuant to agency rules and regulations.
new_rules.notes: Express delegation of waiver grounds to agency (city) rules — fully discretionary; no statutory grounds, purpose test, written-denial duty, or waiver appeal.

new_rules.legal_concept: Alternative fee arrangement for voluminous or frequent requests
new_rules.atomic_rule: An agency may enter into a contract, memorandum of understanding, or other agreement with a requestor providing an alternative fee arrangement to the statutory charges, including in response to a voluminous or frequently occurring request.
new_rules.trigger: Requestor and agency agree to alternative fee terms; or the request is voluminous or frequently occurring.
new_rules.source_language: An agency may enter into any contract, memorandum of understanding, or other agreement with a requestor that provides an alternative fee arrangement to the charges authorized in this section, or in response to a voluminous or frequently occurring request.
new_rules.notes: WA's only repeat/aggregated-requestor fee mechanism — negotiated, not formulaic. Mapped to fee.aggregation as the closest canonical concept (it is the frequent-requestor fee treatment).

new_rules.legal_concept: No fee for inspection or locating records
new_rules.atomic_rule: No fee may be charged for the inspection of public records or for locating public documents and making them available for copying, except for body-worn-camera redaction costs (RCW 42.56.240(14)) and the customized service charge (RCW 42.56.120(3)).
new_rules.trigger: Requestor inspects records, or agency locates records and makes them available for copying.
new_rules.source_language: No fee shall be charged for the inspection of public records or locating public documents and making them available for copying, except as provided in RCW 42.56.240(14) and subsection (3) of this section.
new_rules.notes: Fixed at zero: search/retrieval and inspection labor categorically non-chargeable. This is the rule that makes labor.search.rate not_applicable in WA.

new_rules.legal_concept: Summary of charges on request before copying
new_rules.atomic_rule: If a requestor asks, the agency shall provide a summary of the applicable charges before any copies are made, and the requestor may revise the request to reduce the number of copies and the charges.
new_rules.trigger: Requestor asks for a summary of applicable charges.
new_rules.source_language: A requestor may ask an agency to provide, and if requested an agency shall provide, a summary of the applicable charges before any copies are made and the requestor may revise the request to reduce the number of copies to be made and reduce the applicable charges.
new_rules.notes: On-request duty with no dollar threshold — WA's version of the cost-notice gate. Restated in AG model rule WAC 44-14-07001(5) (advisory guidance).

new_rules.atomic_rule: A law enforcement or corrections agency may require a requester not exempt under RCW 42.56.240(14)(e) to pay the reasonable costs of redacting or obscuring portions of a body-worn-camera recording before disclosure, only to the extent required by applicable exemptions, using the least costly commercially available redaction method to the extent possible and reasonable.
new_rules.trigger: Request for body worn camera recordings from a law enforcement or corrections agency by a requester not listed in RCW 42.56.240(14)(e).
new_rules.source_language: A law enforcement or corrections agency responding to a request to disclose body worn camera recordings may require any requester not listed in (e) of this subsection to pay the reasonable costs of redacting, altering, distorting, pixelating, suppressing, or otherwise obscuring any portion of the body worn camera recording prior to disclosure only to the extent necessary to comply with the exemptions in this chapter or any applicable law.
new_rules.notes: The exception RCW 42.56.120(1) points to. Applies to law-enforcement/corrections agencies only (municipal police included). Exempt requesters per (14)(e): persons directly involved in the incident, their attorneys, and certain others. (14)(f)(iii): redaction time does not count against any local time/cost allocation for records responses. Section amended through 2026 c 174; text extracted from the official RCW page via retrieval tool (two consistent fetches) — flag for verify-pass confirmation against certified text.

new_rules.legal_concept: Cost statement adopted only after notice and public hearing
new_rules.atomic_rule: An agency's statement of actual copying costs (and the factors and manner used to determine them) may be adopted only after providing notice and a public hearing.
new_rules.trigger: Agency adopts or amends its statement of actual costs for copies.
new_rules.source_language: Each agency may establish, maintain, and make available for public inspection and copying a statement of the actual costs that it charges for providing photocopies or electronically produced copies, of public records and a statement of the factors and manner used to determine the actual costs. Any statement of costs may be adopted by an agency only after providing notice and public hearing.
new_rules.notes: Adoption-procedure gate on the city's own fee schedule; WA-0027 quoted only the first sentence — the notice-and-hearing sentence is the operative addition here. Verbatim from the certified 7/15/2026 PDF.

new_rules.legal_concept: Copy-and-send staff time includable in actual costs
new_rules.atomic_rule: Staff time to copy and send the requested public records may be included in an agency's actual copying costs; staff salaries, benefits, and general overhead otherwise may not be included unless directly related to the actual cost of copying.
new_rules.trigger: Agency calculates its actual costs for providing copies.
new_rules.source_language: In determining the actual costs for providing copies of public records, an agency may not include staff salaries, benefits, or other general administrative or overhead charges, unless those costs are directly related to the actual cost of copying the public records. Staff time to copy and send the requested public records may be included in an agency's costs.
new_rules.notes: The only generally chargeable labor in WA: copy-and-send time, folded into the published actual-cost calculation (no standalone hourly rate). Verbatim from the certified 7/15/2026 PDF; the final sentence was absent from WA-0028.

new_rules.legal_concept: Actual cost of media, container, and postage
new_rules.atomic_rule: Under the default schedule, an agency may charge the actual cost of any digital storage media or device it provides, the actual cost of any container or envelope used to mail the copies, and the actual postage or delivery charge.
new_rules.trigger: Copies are provided on agency-supplied media or mailed to the requestor.
new_rules.source_language: The actual cost of any digital storage media or device provided by the agency, the actual cost of any container or envelope used to mail the copies to the requestor, and the actual postage or delivery charge.
new_rules.notes: Basis is 'actual cost' passed through (no numeric ceiling). Charges under 120(2)(b) may be combined when more than one type applies (120(2)(c)). Covers both the media item (CD/DVD/USB) and mail delivery.

delegations_followed.instrument: Agency-published statement of actual costs (each agency's own, adopted after notice and public hearing)
delegations_followed.instrument_cite: Local instrument — per-agency statement of costs
delegations_followed.figures_extracted: None — the delegated instrument is each city's OWN published cost statement, not a state schedule; there is no statewide instrument to open. The statute's default ceilings (15c/10c/5c-per-4-files/10c-per-GB/$2 flat) govern absent a local statement.

delegations_followed.instrument: AG model rules on public records charges, chapter 44-14 WAC
delegations_followed.figures_extracted: No figures beyond the statute — WAC 44-14-07001 restates the RCW 42.56.120 charges, including the mandatory on-request summary of charges (subsection (5)). Model rules are advisory guidance for agencies, not binding law.

applicability_notes: Chapter 42.56 RCW defines 'agency' to include every state and local agency, so all fee provisions here bind municipalities directly — WA runs ONE regime for state and local bodies (no separate state-agency uniform fee schedule); applies_to = all_public_bodies throughout.
RCW 42.56.240(14)(f) (body-cam redaction costs) applies only to law enforcement and corrections agencies — for a city this means the police department function, not general municipal records.

The 'delegated instrument' pattern in WA points inward: the statute delegates the operative actual-cost figures to each agency's OWN published statement of costs (adopted after notice and public hearing), which is exactly the city configuration this product generates — recorded as ceiling/actual-cost resolutions, not delegated_unresolved.
AG model rules (chapter 44-14 WAC) are advisory for agencies; cited only as the guidance layer, never as the source of a figure.
material_negatives: No graduated page bands, free-page allowance, free-labor-hours, or periodic per-requestor free time — the default rates are flat per-unit ceilings.
No labor billing increment/rounding rule (largely moot: hourly labor billing barely exists in WA).
No dollar/hour threshold for a mandatory cost estimate — the summary-of-charges duty is on-request (120(2)(f)), plus a mandatory pre-charge notice for customized service charges (120(3)(b)).
No requester response window, estimate validity period, or estimate-overrun revision percentage anywhere in the fee sections, RCW 42.56.520, or WAC 44-14-07001.
No deposit dollar threshold (deposit allowed for any request, capped at 10% of estimate) and no statutory clock effect, grace period, or lapse action while a deposit is unpaid.

No de-minimis floor, no minimum fee (the $2 flat fee is a capped optional alternative, not a minimum), no certification fee in the PRA, and no commercial-purpose fee schedule (commercial list requests are prohibited, not surcharged).
No fee forfeiture on late response — WA late-response consequences are penalties/attorney fees under RCW 42.56.550, outside fee scope.
Overhead/fringe surcharges are affirmatively PROHIBITED in the actual-cost calculation (070(7)(b)) — a prohibition, not mere silence.
